method: Effective starting stalls after scratchings where known; published handicap weights unless a documented carried-weight exception; Cup-specific running position from reported evidence, not lifetime style. Why notes are retrospective interpretation.

years.race_story: A strong tempo helped the late runners. Dunaden and Red Cadeaux came from the back and fought out an exceptionally close photo. Lucas Cranach struck the front around 400m out but was overrun; defending champion Americain recovered from a poor start and wide run to finish fourth under 58kg.

top4.run_style: Backmarker — observed in this Cup; not a fixed habitual classification
top4.history: Won the Geelong Cup over 2400m 13 days earlier; had established European staying form.
top4.why: A fast pace gave his late run time to develop; he caught Red Cadeaux in a nose photo.

top4.run_style: Backmarker — observed in this Cup; not a fixed habitual classification
top4.history: English-trained international stayer; later also ran second in the 2013 and 2014 Cups.
top4.why: Came wide from the rear in a fast-run race and was beaten by the narrowest of margins.

top4.run_style: Midfield with cover — planned by jockey beforehand; good run and move from 600m confirmed after the Cup
top4.history: Fifth in the 2400m Caulfield Cup at his previous start.
top4.why: Brown reported a perfect run, moved from 600m and hit the front in the straight, but two stronger late finishers overhauled him.

top4.run_style: Backmarker — observed toward rear in this Cup
top4.history: Won the 2010 Melbourne Cup and the 2011 Moonee Valley Cup; arrived as the favourite.
top4.why: Despite settling back, a wide turn and the 58kg topweight, finished just behind Lucas Cranach; Mosse said firm ground also counted against him.

years.race_story: Glencadam Gold and Mourayan led, but the middle stages were moderate and the field sprinted home; this disadvantaged deep backmarkers. Green Moon secured position, took over in the straight and held Fiorente by a length; Jakkalberry closed for third and Kelinni stayed on for fourth.

top4.run_style: Handy/midfield — observed in this Cup after an early check pushed him to the rail
top4.history: Previously won a Newcastle Gold Cup and placed in the 2011 Caulfield Cup; won Group 1 races in 2012 but was seventh in the Cox Plate ten days earlier.
top4.why: Prebble saved ground and was close enough when the race became a sprint; he accelerated clear from the turn.

top4.run_style: Midfield/late runner — inferred from working home behind Green Moon; exact early position unverified
top4.history: First Australian start after arriving from Britain; went on to win this race in 2013.
top4.why: Saved ground from barrier 2 and finished strongly but could not catch a winner already clear in the sprint home.

top4.run_style: Late runner — inferred from his run into third; exact early position unverified
top4.history: Won the American St Leger over 2700m, then was 13th in the Caulfield Cup after interference; had a Group 1 placing in Dubai.
top4.why: Showed international staying quality and recovered from a poor Caulfield Cup run to close from a wide draw.

top4.run_style: Handy/midfield — inferred from challenging near Green Moon in the straight; exact early position unverified
top4.history: Won the Lexus/Hotham Handicap over 2500m on Derby Day to earn a Cup start three days later.
top4.why: The light 51kg and fitness from a fresh staying win helped him hold fourth in a race that penalised deep closers.

years.data_note: Jakkalberry is shown at 55.5kg in contemporaneous fields and result reports; one Racing Australia table prints 55kg.

years.race_story: Ruscello and Tres Blue set a hard early tempo. Damien Oliver rode Fiorente patiently and advanced on the turn. Red Cadeaux travelled midfield with cover despite gate 23 and briefly looked the winner; Fiorente ran him down. Mount Athos had worked forward from gate 22 and held third, with Simenon staying into fourth.

top4.run_style: Midfield/held up patiently — observed in this Cup
top4.history: Second in the 2012 Cup; third in the Cox Plate immediately before this win.
top4.why: Strong early pace helped the patient ride, and Oliver advanced smoothly on the turn before outfinishing Red Cadeaux.

top4.run_style: Midfield with cover — jockey's race-day account
top4.history: Second in the 2011 Cup, eighth in 2012; proven at 3200m.
top4.why: Mosse found cover despite the outside gate; Red Cadeaux kicked clear before Fiorente caught him late.

top4.run_style: Forward/midfield — observed close to front after working across from wide draw
top4.history: Fifth in the 2012 Cup; established European stayer with wins around 2800m.
top4.why: Williams overcame gate 22 to get a position; the horse stayed on for third despite the early work.

top4.run_style: Habitual hold-up runner per Hong Kong Jockey Club; early settling position in this Cup unverified, but jockey reported travelling well at 800m
top4.history: Second in the Ascot Gold Cup over 4000m and Lonsdale Cup over 3300m; third in the Herbert Power Stakes over 2400m.
top4.why: Proven extreme stamina enabled him to keep finishing after losing a length when the field quickened.

years.race_story: A very strong early tempo made stamina decisive. Protectionist saved ground in midfield on the rail, then found a gap and surged four lengths clear. Red Cadeaux reached the lead in the straight and held second from the finishing Who Shot Thebarman. Signoff was around tenth in running and finished fourth.

top4.run_style: Midfield on rail — observed in this Cup
top4.history: Won the Prix Kergorlay over 3000m in France; fourth in the Herbert Power Stakes at his Australian lead-up.
top4.why: Saved ground behind a strong pace, then showed the strongest sustained finish when Moore found a gap.

top4.run_style: Midfield, around seventh one off rail — observed in this Cup
top4.history: Already twice runner-up in the Cup (2011 and 2013); this was his fourth attempt.
top4.why: Advanced with cover and led in the straight; dug in for second despite a high weight and Protectionist's finishing burst.

top4.run_style: Midfield, around tenth on rail — observed in this Cup
top4.history: Won the Auckland Cup over 3200m and The Bart Cummings over 2500m; had been 13th in the Caulfield Cup.
top4.why: Returned to the roomier Flemington track, saved ground and advanced between runners to reach third near 300m.

top4.run_style: Midfield, around tenth — observed in this Cup
top4.history: Won the Lexus/Hotham Handicap over 2500m three days earlier to enter the Cup; first try at 3200m.
top4.why: Lightweight and recent Flemington staying win supported a fourth; was bumped before the turn and could not match Protectionist's late burst.

years.data_note: Signoff was allotted 51kg but actually carried 51.5kg. The row shows the carried weight.

years.race_story: Big Orange led a moderate early pace. Prince Of Penzance saved ground in about tenth on the rail, followed Trip To Paris into the straight and sprinted through to beat Max Dynamite by half a length. Criterion enjoyed a close trail and finished third; Trip To Paris raced fourth early and held fourth.

top4.run_style: Midfield, about tenth on rail — observed in this Cup
top4.history: Won the 2014 Moonee Valley Gold Cup over 2500m; second in the same race in 2015 after a lengthy spell.
top4.why: Barrier 1 allowed a ground-saving run, and Payne found a clear path following Trip To Paris before an explosive finish.

top4.run_style: Midfield/in touch — race report places him around tenth 400m out
top4.history: Won the Lonsdale Cup over about 3300m at York; first Australian run.
top4.why: Proven long-distance stamina powered a late finish despite being blocked and switched wide late.

top4.run_style: Handy, about fifth — observed in this Cup
top4.history: Group 1-class runner; second in the Cox Plate immediately beforehand, with European Group 1 experience earlier in 2015.
top4.why: A close, economical trail kept him in contention; carried a heavy 57.5kg and stayed on for third.

top4.run_style: Handy, about fourth — observed in this Cup
top4.history: Won the Ascot Gold Cup over about 4000m; second in the Caulfield Cup at his Australian lead-up.
top4.why: Had a good forward run at a gentle pace and used proven staying stamina to hold fourth, though the winner came off his back.

years.race_story: Excess Knowledge and others set a searching tempo. Almandin and Heartbreak City settled well back (about 15th-18th for much of the race), then swept past Hartnell and fought out a close two-horse finish. Hartnell was sixth at the turn and held third; Qewy raced in the top third throughout and held fourth.

top4.run_style: Backmarker — observed around 15th-18th through middle stages
top4.history: Won The Bart Cummings over 2500m at Flemington one month earlier; previously Group 2 winner in Germany.
top4.why: McEvoy conserved him behind a strong pace, then produced a sustained outside run; 52kg helped him outlast Heartbreak City.

top4.run_style: Backmarker — observed around 14th-16th through middle stages
top4.history: Won the Ebor Handicap over about 2800m at York at previous start; experienced flat and hurdle stayer.
top4.why: Moreira settled him despite the wide gate, made one sustained move and briefly led at 250m before Almandin prevailed.

top4.run_style: Midfield — observed just ahead of backmarkers and sixth at turn
top4.history: Won the Turnbull Stakes and was runner-up to Winx in the Cox Plate immediately beforehand; top-class Group 1 performer.
top4.why: Travelled well and had the class to hold third, but the 3200m and 56kg blunted his final sprint against the lighter first two.

top4.run_style: On pace/top third — observed throughout this Cup
top4.history: Won the Geelong Cup over 2400m, leading all the way; had European long-distance flat and hurdle form.
top4.why: Kept grinding from a forward position under 51.5kg and outstayed the pack contesting fourth.

years.data_note: The Racing Australia Fact Book barrier column appears to repeat saddlecloths for Heartbreak City, Hartnell and Qewy; contemporaneous starting gates are used.

years.race_story: Cismontane led at a casual early pace, with speed increasing from halfway. Johannes Vermeer sat close behind the leaders and struck the front at 300m. Rekindling saved ground midfield on the inside, then chased him down with 51.5kg. Max Dynamite had a rail run and finished third; Big Duke was fourth.

top4.run_style: Midfield on rail — observed in this Cup
top4.history: Won the Curragh Cup over 2800m, second in the Irish St Leger Trial and fourth in the Doncaster St Leger; first Australian race.
top4.why: A ground-saving run from gate 4 and a very light weight gave him enough late speed to catch Johannes Vermeer.

top4.run_style: Handy/forward midfield, around fifth — observed in this Cup
top4.history: Second in the Caulfield Stakes over 2000m and third in the Caulfield Cup over 2400m, where he had trouble getting clear.
top4.why: Gate 3 let him race near the pace, he led at 300m, then 51.5kg Rekindling caught him near the line.

top4.run_style: Midfield, around seventh on rail — observed in this Cup
top4.history: Second in the 2015 Melbourne Cup; returned from injury and won a 3400m race at Killarney in 2017.
top4.why: Gate 2 gave a ground-saving rail run and his proven 3200m form helped him finish third.

top4.run_style: Midfield — observed in this Cup; followed Rekindling into the straight
top4.history: Won the Launceston Cup, Manion Cup and Chairman's Handicap; second in The Metropolitan, won the ATC St Leger over 2600m, then fourth in the Moonee Valley Gold Cup after traffic trouble.
top4.why: A strong domestic staying campaign and a good trail supported fourth; his jockey said he ran out of gas in the straight.

years.race_story: Runaway and Vengeur Masque led early, with Finche prominent. Cross Counter sat near the rear and came wide to run down Marmelo, who had taken over from Prince Of Arran late. The rain-affected ground and a 51 kg handicap accompanied the winner’s fast finish.

top4.run_style: Backmarker; near rear, wide late
top4.history: Won the 2018 Gordon Stakes (about 2400 m) and was second in the Great Voltigeur before his first Australian start.
top4.why: His late acceleration from near the rear, with only 51 kg, overhauled Marmelo inside the final 100 m.

top4.run_style: Backmarker; third-last for much of race
top4.history: Won the 2018 Grand Cup (2770 m) and Prix Maurice de Nieuil (2800 m); had finished ninth in the 2017 Cup after trying to lead.
top4.why: Relaxed near the rear and came through inside to challenge strongly, but Cross Counter swept past late.
top4.weight_note: 55 kg is published handicap. Bowman weighed in more than 0.5 kg above it; exact in-race burden not verifiable from these sources.

top4.run_style: Prominent; moved to front in straight
top4.history: Won the 2500 m Lexus/Hotham Stakes three days earlier after a Herbert Power placing; had already raced successfully at 3200 m.
top4.why: His recent local staying win and forward position put him in front in the straight; Marmelo and Cross Counter finished faster.

top4.run_style: On pace; among early leaders
top4.history: Won the 2018 Prix de Reux (2500 m) in France; ran in Australia after joining Chris Waller.
top4.why: Raced close to the lead and was still in the contest at 300 m, then held fourth as the late closers passed.

years.data_note: Marmelo is listed at the published 55kg handicap; a post-race report says the jockey weighed in more than 0.5kg above it.

years.race_story: Vow And Declare jumped well from a wide stall, crossed to the rail and then ceded the lead. The pace was slow. Master Of Reality raced outside the leader and surged clear in the straight, but Vow And Declare came back on the rail. Prince Of Arran and Il Paradiso closed. Master Of Reality crossed second but a sustained protest demoted him to fourth for interference to Il Paradiso.

top4.run_style: Forward/rail; ceded lead
top4.history: Second in the 2019 Caulfield Cup (2400 m); won a Listed Flemington race the previous Cup carnival.
top4.why: Williams neutralised gate 21 by pressing forward, then saved ground on the rail and rallied to win a blanket finish.

top4.run_style: Prominent; tracked Master Of Reality
top4.history: Third in the 2018 Cup; won the 2019 Geelong Cup on his final lead-up.
top4.why: Tracked a strong on-pace rival for most of the race and finished on; promoted to second after protest.

top4.run_style: Backmarker; third-last early
top4.history: Third in the 2019 Lonsdale Cup over about 3200 m; fifth in the English St Leger.
top4.why: Produced the fastest last 800 m and last 400 m after a slow early pace, but was impeded late; promoted from fourth to third.

top4.run_style: On pace; outside leader
top4.history: Third in the 2019 Ascot Gold Cup over about 4000 m, showing proven marathon stamina.
top4.why: His front-running stamina nearly held off the field after a slow tempo; crossed second but was demoted for interference.

years.race_story: Twilight Payment controlled the race from the front at a strong tempo. Tiger Moth crossed from a wide draw to race beside or behind him and challenged late. Prince Of Arran was held up behind weakening horses before finishing rapidly; The Chosen One challenged at the 400 m but could not match the first three late.

top4.run_style: Leader; led throughout
top4.history: Won the Curragh Cup (2800 m) in 2020; had run 11th in the 2019 Melbourne Cup.
top4.why: McNeil set and managed the pace from the lead, then the proven stayer kept finding enough to resist Tiger Moth.

top4.run_style: On pace; outside leader early
top4.history: Runner-up in the 2020 Irish Derby (2400 m); the Cup was just his fifth career start and first attempt beyond 2400 m.
top4.why: McEvoy crossed from gate 22 and travelled close to the leader despite the extra ground, then kept chasing to finish within half a length.

top4.run_style: Covered trip; trapped, then late closer
top4.run_style_basis: observed covered trip, early rank not verified
top4.history: Third in the 2018 Cup and second in 2019; entered with 2020 Caulfield Cup fourth.
top4.why: Barrier 1 gave cover but also led to a blocked passage behind tiring runners; once clear at 350 m he recorded the race’s fastest closing 400 m.

top4.run_style: Midfield type expected; challenged at 400 m
top4.run_style_basis: pre-race midfield expectation plus observed move at 400 m; exact early Cup position not verified
top4.history: Third in the 2020 Caulfield Cup over 2400 m; had finished 17th in the 2019 Melbourne Cup.
top4.why: The low gate provided an economical run; he was travelling strongly on the bend and kept fourth despite weakening against the first three late.

years.race_story: Persan led and Incentivise sat second. Verry Elleegant settled midfield three wide with cover, advanced on the turn, passed Incentivise and won by four lengths. Spanish Mission and Floating Artist were close behind the runner-up.

top4.run_style: Midfield, three wide with cover
top4.history: Nine Group 1 wins before the Cup, including the 2020 Caulfield Cup; had been seventh in the 2020 Melbourne Cup.
top4.why: Her class and covered midfield ride let her sustain a long run, overcoming 57 kg and the outer half of the draw.

top4.run_style: On pace; second behind leader
top4.history: Won the 2021 Caulfield Cup after a long winning sequence; the Cup was his first attempt at 3200 m.
top4.why: Crossed from gate 15 to a forward spot and still held second under 57 kg, though Verry Elleegant passed him decisively.

top4.run_style: Midfield; moved forward late
top4.history: Won the 2021 Yorkshire Cup over about 2800 m and ran a close second to Stradivarius in the Lonsdale Cup.
top4.why: Proven staying form and a midfield trip kept him competitive; he moved up with the main challengers but could not match the winner.

top4.run_style: On pace
top4.run_style_basis: observed, Racing and Sports result comment
top4.history: Runner-up in the Moonee Valley Cup (2500 m) at his previous start after a consistent local preparation.
top4.why: His forward run and minimum 50 kg put him in contention at the 400 m; he kept fourth at his first 3200 m attempt.

years.race_story: Serpentine and Knights Order pushed the early pace. Gold Trip settled worse than midfield, swept around and took control in the straight, holding off Emissary. High Emocean came from near last for third; well-fancied Deauville Legend travelled closer to the pace, looked poised turning in, then faded to fourth.

top4.run_style: Back half; sweeping late run
top4.history: Runner-up in the 2022 Caulfield Cup and ninth in the Cox Plate after high-class French form.
top4.why: Overcame the top weight with a sustained run in a strongly run, wet-track Cup; he went past Deauville Legend and held Emissary.

top4.run_style: Midfield on rail; moved off at 800 m
top4.history: Won the 2022 Geelong Cup (2400 m) at his previous start; had not previously raced beyond 2500 m.
top4.why: Moloney saved ground from gate 3, avoided tired runners at the 800 m and challenged in the straight; he could not sustain it past Gold Trip.

top4.run_style: Backmarker; near last, strong late
top4.history: Won the 2022 Bendigo Cup (2400 m) six days before the Melbourne Cup; carried just 50 kg.
top4.why: The stayer finished strongly from near the rear and passed Deauville Legend late for third.

top4.run_style: Handy; fourth approaching turn
top4.history: Won the 2022 Great Voltigeur Stakes (2400 m) in Britain; this was his first 3200 m attempt.
top4.why: A prominent, economical trip gave him first run, but he was outstayed by Gold Trip, Emissary and High Emocean in the Soft 7 finish.

years.race_story: Serpentine helped set a solid tempo. Without A Fight dropped back from gate 16, found cover and clear running, then drew away to win by more than two lengths. Soulcombe missed the start by several lengths but ran second. Sheraz and Ashrun stayed on for third and fourth, with Ashrun coming from 17th in running and held up briefly before the straight.

top4.run_style: Backmarker; covered, then threaded through
top4.history: Won the 2023 Caulfield Cup; had finished 13th in the wet 2022 Cup.
top4.why: The firmer track and covered back-half run suited him; Zahra found a path off the home turn and the horse accelerated clear.

top4.run_style: Backmarker after missing start
top4.history: Won the 2022 Queen Elizabeth Stakes (2500 m) at Flemington and was third in the 2023 Turnbull Stakes.
top4.why: Despite a slow start, he closed strongly behind the winner; barrier 4 did not yield an inside forward position.

top4.run_style: Backmarker expected; Cup early position not verified
top4.history: Won a French 3000 m Listed race in 2021; runner-up in the 2022 Sydney Cup (3200 m), confirming distance stamina.
top4.why: His proven two-mile stamina and light 51.5 kg are relevant to the surprise third; available reports do not isolate a specific barrier or pace advantage.

top4.run_style: Backmarker; 17th in running, late closer
top4.history: Won the 2020 Hotham Stakes (2500 m), returned after a tendon injury, and was second in the 2023 Geelong Cup.
top4.why: Worked home from 17th despite a brief hold-up around 400–300 m; known staying form and 51.5 kg helped him hold fourth.

years.race_story: Just Fine led early then faded. Knight’s Choice was farther back than intended, saved ground around the turn and closed along the inside. Warp Speed also came from the rear to be beaten a nose. Okita Soushi raced handy and led near 200 m; Zardozi had a midfield trip and briefly challenged. Athabascan was scratched, so these are effective starting gates, one lower than several published draws.

top4.run_style: Backmarker; ground-saving late closer
top4.history: Last won a Doomben 2000 m handicap in December 2023; came into the Cup off 14th in the 2024 Caulfield Cup and an improved fifth in the Bendigo Cup.
top4.why: Dolan conserved ground after settling well back and found an inside run; the 51.5 kg outsider caught Warp Speed on the line.

top4.run_style: Backmarker; late outer run
top4.history: Japanese 3200 m form included fifth in the Tenno Sho (Spring) before arriving in Australia; Caulfield Cup 2400 m was too short for his staying profile.
top4.why: He settled back despite an inside gate and sustained a wide late challenge, beaten only a nose. Weight verified at 54.5 kg by Racing and Sports.

top4.run_style: Handy/on pace
top4.history: Won the 2024 Moonee Valley Gold Cup (2500 m) before this, improving on his 11th in the 2023 Melbourne Cup.
top4.why: Kah positioned him near the front and he took over around 200 m; he held third after the two backmarkers swept through.

top4.run_style: Midfield; challenged in straight
top4.history: Won the 2023 VRC Oaks (2500 m), then second in the 2024 Metropolitan (2400 m) and fifth in the Empire Rose on Derby Day.
top4.why: A smooth midfield trip and low weight put her in contention, but Atzeni said she did not fully see out the 3200 m.

years.race_story: The pace was moderate at first, then Land Legend accelerated to the lead mid-race and stretched the field. Half Yours settled midfield, remained patient, found an inside run and won by 2.75 lengths. Goodie Two Shoes raced off the pace and briefly looked the winner; Middle Earth ran from midfield; River Of Stars held on from sixth.

top4.run_style: Midfield; inside late run
top4.history: Won the 2025 Caloundra Cup (2400 m), then the Caulfield Cup (2400 m) with a 2 kg penalty taking him to 53 kg for Flemington.
top4.why: Melham waited when the pace lifted, secured an inside gap and drew clear; his recent elite staying form translated to 3200 m.

top4.run_style: Off pace; one off rail
top4.history: Won three staying stakes races in Ireland in 2025 and was third in the Lillie Langtry Stakes (2800 m).
top4.why: Lordan found cover despite gate 20; she travelled into the straight and led around 300 m before Half Yours passed her.

top4.run_style: Midfield; wide home turn
top4.history: Won the 2024 Aston Park Stakes (2400 m); a fair 2025 Caulfield Cup was followed by an improved JRA Cup run with blinkers.
top4.why: The improved lead-up continued: he quickened from midfield and briefly challenged at 300 m, but could not sustain the effort to the line.

top4.run_style: Handy; settled sixth
top4.history: Third in the 2025 Sydney Cup (3200 m), then third in the Caulfield Cup; she dropped 2 kg for Flemington.
top4.why: Proven two-mile stamina and a handy trip let her stay on for fourth, though she lacked the winner’s turn of foot.
